clues: This city sits in the middle of Florida, on a main road east of Tampa. It lies a bit south west of Orlando too.
This warm city still gets a sharp cold snap most years. Twice a year, on average, its air drops below the point where water turns to ice.
Rail lines reached this town in the 1880s and town life grew fast. The first Black rail workers made their homes here in 1883.
All the swans on its lakes come from just two birds. Queen Elizabeth the Second gave that first pair to the city back in 1957.
The head office of Publix, a big grocery chain, stands in this city. That one fact seals it for folks who shop in the south.
